title: UX/UI Designer
description:
Company Overview

APPLICATIONS FROM OUTSIDE CANADA WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED FOR THIS ROLE

Robots & Pencils is an applied AI engineering firm building the next frontier of business architecture. We design and ship AI co-workers that integrate into enterprise operations and deliver measurable results for our clients. We're all in on AWS, combining deep UX capability with senior engineering talent to get AI into production fast and keep it there.

We’ve earned the trust of leaders across Consumer Products and Retail, Education, Energy, Financial Services, Healthcare, and Manufacturing and more, and earned a reputation as the nimble alternative to traditional global systems integrators. Founded in 2009, with delivery centers in Canada, the United States, Eastern Europe, and Latin America, we are smaller, faster, and more senior by design. Our teams average 15+ years of experience. We move fast, sweat the details, and build things that actually ship.

Position Overview

We’re looking for a UX/UI Designer to design thoughtful, high-quality digital experiences across a range of client engagements. This role is ideal for a curious, collaborative designer who enjoys solving real problems and bringing ideas to life — from early concepts through polished delivery.

In this role, you will partner closely with client product teams and our internal team to turn complex ideas into clear, intuitive, and engaging experiences. You’ll be joining real, in-flight work where quality and delivery speed matter, collaborating with experienced designers and growing the instincts that come from shipping things that matter.

Why This Role Matters

At Robots & Pencils, we design AI systems for a human world. Our name says it all. Robots and pencils means engineering paired with creativity, because every agent we ship has to work for real people in real workflows. That balance is baked into how we operate.

Every role here contributes directly to that mission. Here, you shape how AI systems integrate into enterprise operations, how teams move at real velocity, and how products create measurable impact for clients and the people they serve. We ship production-ready AI in 30 to 45 days. That pace demands people who take ownership, lead with craft, and care deeply about what they put their name on.

What You’ll Do

Craft & Delivery

• Design end-to-end UX/UI deliverables from early exploration and concepting through high-fidelity execution

• Create wireframes, prototypes, and polished interface designs that balance usability, business goals, and technical constraints

• Build, evolve, and maintain design systems that support consistency, scalability, and flexibility across products

• Conduct UX research activities including usability testing and user interviews to inform design decisions

• Use Figma confidently for design, prototyping, documentation, and collaboration

• Bring an AI-forward mindset to your design work, using tools like Figma AI and Claude to improve efficiency, creativity, and design quality

Collaboration & Communication

• Partner closely with client product teams to understand problems, shape solutions, and deliver meaningful outcomes

• Collaborate with engineers, strategists, and delivery leads to bring designs to life effectively and efficiently

• Participate in agile workflows and balance multiple projects, clients, and industries while maintaining a high bar for craft

Leadership & Influence

• Take ownership of design work end-to-end and follow through with craft and consistency

• Contribute to internal initiatives such as marketing, pitches, and the evolution of the design practice

• Stay curious and keep growing — bring new ideas, experiment often, and embrace continuous improvement

What You’ll Bring

• 2+ years of professional experience as a UX/UI Designer working on digital products or platforms

• Strong hands-on design skills with deep proficiency in Figma

• Experience building and maintaining design systems in real-world product environments

• Working knowledge of UX research methods including usability testing and user interviews

• Experience working directly with clients or cross-functional product teams

• A collaborative mindset with comfort giving and receiving design feedback

• Ability to adapt to design approaches across different industries, users, and problem spaces

• Curiosity and enthusiasm for AI-assisted design tools and workflows (e.g., Figma AI, Claude)

• Experience with motion design, advanced prototyping tools, front-end concepts, or workshop facilitation is a plus

You’ll Do Well Here if You Are

•
A doer. You see something broken and fix it. You'd rather move on clarity than wait for certainty.

•
A fast learner who knows you don't know everything. The AI landscape changes weekly. You're senior enough to know better and curious enough to keep learning anyway.

•
Direct in a way that makes the work better. You give honest feedback. You'd rather have the hard conversation than blow smoke.

•
Obsessed with craft. You know genius is in the details. You ship exceptional, not perfect, and you don't put your name on work you wouldn't stand behind.

•
Built for ownership. You honor commitments, admit mistakes fast, and back your teammates when a decision costs something. No handoffs, no finger-pointing.

•
All in. You treat clients' businesses like your own. You take the work seriously without taking yourself seriously.

•
Resourceful when the budget, timeline, or team is tight. Constraints don't slow you down. They sharpen you.

•
Glad to be in the room with people who care as much as you do. Our teams average fifteen-plus years of experience. We hire people who push each other to do better work.

Your current employer will not be contacted without your permission.  We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

title: Lead UX Designer
description:
Job Overview

Team: Ivans UX

Salary Range: $120,000-$165,000 USD

Location: Remote US and Canada

Opportunity for Impact

Ivans, a division of Applied Systems, is where insurance technology gets reinvented, and we build it fast. Our cloud software and AI-powered solutions reach thousands of agencies and brokers worldwide, setting the pace for what modern insurance can do.

We’re looking for a Lead UX Designer to join our UX team. This person will be designing complex, multi-step, high-volume workflows that insurance agents will use over and over. Success will result in removing time, friction, and errors. The Lead UX Designer will shape strategic direction for this major initiative, providing product vision and leadership to this critical initiative.

What You’ll Do

Planning and Process

• Defines UX strategies and frameworks for multi‑team initiatives.

• Leads planning sessions to align scope, timeline, and success metrics across disciplines.

• Ensures UX activities connect seamlessly to product and business roadmaps.

UX Research

• Shapes research agendas and ensures insights and tangible success metrics drive cross‑product decisions.

• Integrates data from multiple sources to inform strategic design direction.

• Guides research prioritization and alignment across teams or product lines.

Information Architecture

• Creates scalable IA frameworks and models that span multiple workflows and systems.

• Aligns content structures and naming conventions across teams for consistency.

• Validates navigation frameworks through iterative testing and stakeholder review.

Interaction Design

• Designs system‑level interaction models that unify patterns across products.

• Leads development of design frameworks that support reusable experiences.

• Mentors peers in designing for scalability, accessibility, and maintainability.

Visual Design

• Defines visual direction for complex experiences and ensures system alignment.

• Shapes evolution of visual standards within the design system.

• Drives collaboration with engineering and marketing to maintain brand coherence.

Deploying

• Oversees design delivery and implementation planning across product teams.

• Defines and enforces standards for QA, design fidelity, and usability validation.

• Collaborates with engineering leads to improve handoff tools and processes.

Facilitation

• Facilitates high‑impact design workshops and cross‑disciplinary planning sessions.

• Navigates competing priorities and builds alignment through structured discussion.

• Mentors others in effective facilitation and decision‑making practices.

Storytelling

• Delivers compelling design narratives that shape vision and inspire action.

• Translates design strategy into clear, audience‑specific communication.

• Coaches teams in developing storytelling skills for stakeholder alignment.

Key Performance Outcomes

• Execution: Defines and delivers UX strategies that align product vision with user needs and business goals.

• Insights: Applies research & design leadership across complex initiatives, resulting in depth of user understanding and accurate prioritization of highest impact unknowns, and highest business value opportunities.

• Impact: Ensures design consistency across large product areas through system-level thinking and coaching. Raises UX quality through formal and informal mentorship, critique, and design guidance.

What We’re Looking For

• B2B complex interaction design experience, crafting multi-step, high-volume workflows.

• 7+ years of experience in UX/product design, with at least 2 years in a leadership or strategic role.

• Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Design, HCI, or a related discipline — or equivalent senior experience.

• Proven success leading large-scale design efforts with measurable business and user impact.

• Strong portfolio demonstrating design leadership across complex, shipped digital products.

• Deep experience with user research, design systems, and interaction models.

• Expert-level skills in design and collaboration tools (Figma, Miro, etc.).

• Comfortable navigating ambiguity and leading in environments with shifting priorities.

• Mastery of UX design principles, systems thinking, interaction models, and product strategy alignment.

• Exceptional facilitation and communication skills; able to influence senior stakeholders and guide decision-making.

• Deep understanding of research methodologies and their strategic application.

• Ability to coach designers through complex problem spaces and grow team capability.

• Experience working across multiple product domains or platforms.

• Knowledge of technical constraints and development workflows; collaborates effectively with engineering.

• Experience working across multiple product domains and stakeholder groups.

Bonus points if you also have:

• Visionary thinking with the ability to drive long-term design impact while delivering in the short term.

Talent shows up in a lot of different ways, and we mean that. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experience levels, including military members and their spouses and those without a traditional degree or tech background. If this role speaks to you, apply.

Why You’ll Like Working on Team Applied

The best work happens when smart people move fast, together. For over 40+ years, Applied has built technology that solves real problems for insurance professionals - and we’re still pushing what’s possible.

You’ll be part of our people-first culture built on trust, inclusion, and growth - where you’re supported to deliver, collaborate with teammates who care, and grow with leaders invested in your success.

How We’ll Support You

We invest in the whole person, not just the role. Our benefits and resources are built to support your health, your time, and your life outside of work:

• Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage

• Holiday and Vacation Time

• Health & Wellness Days

• A Bonus Day for Your Birthday

Compensation Transparency

Our targeted starting base salary in the United States for this position considers a variety of factors, including depth and breadth of experience, skills and role scope. Depending on the role, team members may also be eligible for additional compensation plans (bonus and commission).

Your Security Matters:

Our candidates’ personal information and online safety are top of mind. Applied communicates with candidates only via a secure @appliedsystems.com email address or through our official careers portal. Recruiters will never request payments or ask for financial account or sensitive personal information like Social Security numbers.

AI Utilization

We leverage AI tools to streamline parts of our recruitment workflow (such as resume parsing and interview scheduling). However, final decisions are always conducted by real humans.

EEO Statement

Applied Systems is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. Diversity and Inclusion is a business imperative and is a part of building our brand and reputation. At Applied, we don’t discriminate, and we are committed to recruit, develop, retain, and promote regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law.

description:
Maven Clinic is the world's largest virtual clinic for women and families on a mission to make healthcare work for all of us. Through Maven Enterprise, the company partners with more than 2,300 employers and health plans to provide end-to-end women's and family health programs spanning fertility and family building, maternity and newborn care, parenting and pediatrics, and menopause and midlife — improving clinical outcomes, reducing healthcare costs, and expanding equitable access to high-quality care at scale. Through its consumer platform, Maven provides direct access to virtual care across 30+ specialties, as well as dedicated hormone and GLP-1 care programs purpose-built for women. Founded in 2014 by CEO Kate Ryder, Maven Clinic has raised more than $425 million from leading healthcare and technology investors including General Catalyst, Sequoia, Dragoneer Investment Group, Oak HC/FT, StepStone Group, Icon Ventures, and Lux Capital. Recognized for innovation and industry leadership, Maven has been named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, and FORTUNE Best Places to Work. Learn more at mavenclinic.com

An award-winning culture working towards an important mission – Maven Clinic is a recipient of over 30 workplace and innovation awards, including:

• TIME 100 Most Influential Companies (2023, 2026)

• Fortune Change the World (2024)

• CNBC Disruptor 50 List (2022, 2023, 2024)

• Fortune Best Workplaces for Millennials (2024)

• Fortune Best Workplaces in Health Care (2024)

• Fast Company Most Innovative Companies (2020, 2023)

• Fortune Best Workplaces NY (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

About the role

We have recently launched our direct-to-consumer platform that gives women access to GLP-1 care, hormone care, and 30+ healthcare specialties, connecting metabolic, hormonal, reproductive, mental, and physical health in one care experience. We are building for women who are tired of fragmented care, unclear pricing, limited follow-up, and healthcare experiences that treat each symptom or life stage in isolation.

What You'll Do:

• We’re looking for a founding Product Design Lead to help build and scale Maven’s direct-to-consumer healthcare experiences.

• This role sits at the intersection of consumer growth, healthcare access, product craft, AI-native ways of working, and trust-sensitive design.

• It is a hands-on player-coach role with formal line management responsibility. You’ll lead a small team of senior Product Design/UXR practitioners while also owning high-priority product design work yourself.

• You’ll report to the General Manager, Consumer and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Growth, Data, Clinical, Legal, Operations, and Support teams.

• You will help Maven compete in a fast-moving and highly competitive consumer healthcare market while staying true to what makes Maven different: connected, clinically responsible, whole-person care for women.

• You will be designing for users who are actively comparing options, making decisions quickly, weighing affordability, navigating uncertainty, and deciding whether they trust Maven enough to start and continue care.

• The work will span both 0→1 product development and continuous optimization of live consumer journeys. You’ll help define new journeys, shape concepts, prototype, and bring new consumer healthcare offerings to market, while also improving existing funnels, onboarding, eligibility, pricing, payment, prescription, activation, retention, and cross-sell experiences through research, experimentation, data, and design craft.

What You'll Bring:

• 7+ years of product design experience, including complex consumer product journeys and 0→1 product growth.

• Experience formally managing or leading design teams.

• Strong hands-on product design craft across UX, prototyping, visual design, mobile apps, and responsive web.

• A portfolio showing D2C product design leadership, systems thinking, data-driven decision-making, high-quality execution, and measurable product impact.

title: Lead UX Designer
description:
Job Description

Team: Ivans UX

Salary Range: $120,000-$165,000 USD

Location: Remote US and Canada

Opportunity for Impact

Ivans, a division of Applied Systems, is where insurance technology gets reinvented, and we build it fast. Our cloud software and AI-powered solutions reach thousands of agencies and brokers worldwide, setting the pace for what modern insurance can do.

We’re looking for a Lead UX Designer to join our UX team. This person will be designing complex, multi-step, high-volume workflows that insurance agents will use over and over. Success will result in removing time, friction, and errors. The Lead UX Designer will shape strategic direction for this major initiative, providing product vision and leadership to this critical initiative.

What You’ll Do

Planning and Process

• Defines UX strategies and frameworks for multi‑team initiatives.

• Leads planning sessions to align scope, timeline, and success metrics across disciplines.

• Ensures UX activities connect seamlessly to product and business roadmaps.

UX Research

• Shapes research agendas and ensures insights and tangible success metrics drive cross‑product decisions.

• Integrates data from multiple sources to inform strategic design direction.

• Guides research prioritization and alignment across teams or product lines.

Information Architecture

• Creates scalable IA frameworks and models that span multiple workflows and systems.

• Aligns content structures and naming conventions across teams for consistency.

• Validates navigation frameworks through iterative testing and stakeholder review.

Interaction Design

• Designs system‑level interaction models that unify patterns across products.

• Leads development of design frameworks that support reusable experiences.

• Mentors peers in designing for scalability, accessibility, and maintainability.

Visual Design

• Defines visual direction for complex experiences and ensures system alignment.

• Shapes evolution of visual standards within the design system.

• Drives collaboration with engineering and marketing to maintain brand coherence.

Deploying

• Oversees design delivery and implementation planning across product teams.

• Defines and enforces standards for QA, design fidelity, and usability validation.

• Collaborates with engineering leads to improve handoff tools and processes.

Facilitation

• Facilitates high‑impact design workshops and cross‑disciplinary planning sessions.

• Navigates competing priorities and builds alignment through structured discussion.

• Mentors others in effective facilitation and decision‑making practices.

Storytelling

• Delivers compelling design narratives that shape vision and inspire action.

• Translates design strategy into clear, audience‑specific communication.

• Coaches teams in developing storytelling skills for stakeholder alignment.

Key Performance Outcomes

• Execution: Defines and delivers UX strategies that align product vision with user needs and business goals.

• Insights: Applies research & design leadership across complex initiatives, resulting in depth of user understanding and accurate prioritization of highest impact unknowns, and highest business value opportunities.

• Impact: Ensures design consistency across large product areas through system-level thinking and coaching. Raises UX quality through formal and informal mentorship, critique, and design guidance.

What We’re Looking For

• B2B complex interaction design experience, crafting multi-step, high-volume workflows.

• 7+ years of experience in UX/product design, with at least 2 years in a leadership or strategic role.

• Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Design, HCI, or a related discipline — or equivalent senior experience.

• Proven success leading large-scale design efforts with measurable business and user impact.

• Strong portfolio demonstrating design leadership across complex, shipped digital products.

• Deep experience with user research, design systems, and interaction models.

• Expert-level skills in design and collaboration tools (Figma, Miro, etc.).

• Comfortable navigating ambiguity and leading in environments with shifting priorities.

• Mastery of UX design principles, systems thinking, interaction models, and product strategy alignment.

• Exceptional facilitation and communication skills; able to influence senior stakeholders and guide decision-making.

• Deep understanding of research methodologies and their strategic application.

• Ability to coach designers through complex problem spaces and grow team capability.

• Experience working across multiple product domains or platforms.

• Knowledge of technical constraints and development workflows; collaborates effectively with engineering.

• Experience working across multiple product domains and stakeholder groups.

Bonus points if you also have:

• Visionary thinking with the ability to drive long-term design impact while delivering in the short term.

Talent shows up in a lot of different ways, and we mean that. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experience levels, including military members and their spouses and those without a traditional degree or tech background. If this role speaks to you, apply.

Why You’ll Like Working on Team Applied

The best work happens when smart people move fast, together. For over 40+ years, Applied has built technology that solves real problems for insurance professionals - and we’re still pushing what’s possible.

You’ll be part of our people-first culture built on trust, inclusion, and growth - where you’re supported to deliver, collaborate with teammates who care, and grow with leaders invested in your success.

How We’ll Support You

We invest in the whole person, not just the role. Our benefits and resources are built to support your health, your time, and your life outside of work:

• Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage

• Holiday and Vacation Time

• Health & Wellness Days

• A Bonus Day for Your Birthday

Our targeted starting base salary in the United States for this position considers a variety of factors, including depth and breadth of experience, skills and role scope. Depending on the role, team members may also be eligible for additional compensation plans (bonus and commission).

Your Security Matters:

Applied communicates with candidates only via a secure @appliedsystems.com email address or through our official careers portal. Recruiters will never request payments or ask for financial account or sensitive personal information like Social Security numbers.

AI Utilization

We leverage AI tools to streamline parts of our recruitment workflow (such as resume parsing and interview scheduling). However, final decisions are always conducted by real humans.

EEO Statement

title: Senior Product Designer, AI Platform
description:
About Gladly

For business leaders who want to get AI right, Gladly is the only customer experience AI that delivers the cost savings they need AND the customer devotion that drives lasting business value. With over a decade of singular CX focus and trusted by the world's most customer-centric brands including Crate & Barrel, Breeze Airways, and Ulta Beauty, Gladly was designed for devotion, not deflection: purpose-built to engage customers and turn every conversation into lasting relationship equity. The result is experiences that are radically personal and effortlessly scalable, emotionally intelligent and operationally efficient.

At the heart of our simply powerful platform, Gladly maintains one continuous conversation across all channels while striking the perfect balance of AI and human connection. With 450M+ conversations powered globally, $510M+ cumulative cost savings delivered for customers, and a 65% increase in CSAT, this is a team where your work has real impact at scale. Learn more at.

About the role

You will own product design for the Agent Harness, the part of Gladly AI where teams build, test, launch, monitor, and improve AI agents. Your surface spans both sides of the harness.

• On the side Gladly controls, the agent itself and the channels it works across, your job is helping AI handle more conversations end to end without a human.

• On the side our customers control, the reporting, simulations, and configuration tools brands use to improve their own agents, your job is making every change a customer ships drive more revenue and resolutions.

This is a generalist role where range matters more than depth in any single discipline. In a given week, you might design an eval review workflow, prototype an agent-steering interaction, tighten the design system components that every team consumes, and review UI that shipped without a designer touching it. Much of the product surface at Gladly is now built with AI-assisted tools by engineers and PMs, so a core part of this job is setting and elevating the quality bar for interfaces you didn't author: through the design system, through review, and through taste.

Thoughtful problem-solvers do well here. They dig into the problem before the fix, make their case clearly, and hold strong opinions loosely. The best work usually has more than one mind in it, so we look for designers who seek out other people's ideas and treat them as well as their own.

What you'll own

• End-to-end product design for the Agent Harness: research, flows, interaction design, and visual design for the tools teams use to configure, steer, and evaluate AI agents.

• The shared design library: components, patterns, and guidelines that keep quality high across every team, including teams shipping UI without a dedicated designer.

• Direction on the undefined problems: taking a product area where the direction is still ambiguous, finding the real problem in it, and giving the team something concrete to build toward.

• Design quality across your product areas, including reviewing and elevating AI-generated and engineer-built UI rather than personally producing every screen.

• Prototyping as a first-class design tool: working prototypes, built fast with AI-assisted tooling, used to test ideas with users and align teams before a line of production code is written.

• Designers here shape the practice as well as the product. You'll have real say in the critique rituals, review norms, and craft standards we already run on, and in where they go next.

What we're looking for

• A strong generalist portfolio spanning complex workflow tools, systems thinking, and polished visual craft, ideally including AI product surfaces such as conversational interfaces, agent configuration and oversight tools, or evaluation/observability dashboards.

• Fluency with AI-assisted prototyping and design tooling as part of your daily workflow (going from idea to working prototype in a matter of hours) and a clear point of view on where AI accelerates design work and where human judgment is non-negotiable.

• Experience designing for AI-native products: interfaces where the system's behavior is probabilistic, where trust and steering matter, and where the design problem is as much about legibility and control as about pixels.

• Comfort operating as the design owner for surfaces you didn't personally build: giving crisp, actionable feedback, encoding standards into reusable systems, and raising the bar without being a bottleneck.

• Demonstrated senior-IC judgment: you scope your own work, make progress before the problem is fully defined, carry multiple product areas at once, and operate with minimal oversight.

What this role is not

• This is not a people-management role; it is a senior individual contributor position reporting to the Head of Product.

• This is not a specialist role in a single discipline (pure UX research, pure visual design, or pure design systems); it deliberately spans all of them.

• This is not a brand or marketing design role; it is product design for our AI platform.

Compensation:

$150,000 to $185,000 annual salary + equity + benefits

For cash compensation, we set standard ranges for all U.S.-based roles based on function, level, and geographic location, benchmarked against similar-stage growth companies. In order to be compliant with local legislation, as well as to provide greater transparency to candidates, we share salary ranges on all job postings regardless of desired hiring location. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including geographic location as well as candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Why Join Gladly?

Gladly is redefining customer experience AI; we're designed for devotion, not deflection. We put people at the center of everything we build, from our platform to our culture. When you join us, you'll enjoy:

• Competitive salaries, stock options, and comprehensive benefits

• Generous paid time off, parental leave, and home office stipends

• A fully remote work environment with opportunities for in-person team gatherings

• A strong commitment to professional growth and an inclusive workplace where diverse perspectives thrive

• A company where AI is not a buzzword. We build AI products and we expect our team to use AI tools daily

We're a team that believes in transparency, collaboration, and the idea that the best work happens when talented people genuinely enjoy working together. Top talent, good vibes, no politics. If this role excites you but you don't meet every qualification, we still encourage you to apply. The perspectives and experiences you bring matter more than checking every box.

title: Senior Product Designer

At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About the Product team

The Product team listens to our customers’ needs and translates those insights into a clear product vision. The team works closely with design, engineering, and analytics to build scalable financial products that empower people to manage their money with confidence. We rely on empathy, curiosity, and business sense to prioritize features and improve experiences. Our role is to lead with clarity, support cross-functional execution, and champion the user in every decision.

The role

We’re looking for a Product Designer to join us in supporting our post-purchase experience and international expansion. Design serves a vital role at Affirm: from building narratives through data to creating products that help people make important financial decisions. As a designer, you are responsible for crafting experiences that build trust, confidence and deliver on our principles of honest, transparent financial products.

We’re at a critical inflection point in Affirm’s journey, with millions of people engaging with our products and new opportunities to expand how they use Affirm every day. We’re also growing globally, reaching new customers in new geographies every day.

This Product Designer will help shape our post-purchase experiences, as well as building the next new geographies that Affirm will expand into. You can demonstrate a breadth of design experience leveraging your ability to create delightful experiences that simplify our customers’ payment management experience through Affirm as well as contributing to our wider international expansion strategy. You’ll partner well with design leadership, design research, and content design. You’ll work end-to-end, from contributing towards Design and Product vision to delivering class leading design. You are able to work closely with Product and Engineering to tailor unique customer experiences for our merchants & consumers while ensuring cohesion to the core Affirm experience - championing our customers needs no matter where their journey starts.

What You'll Do

•
Lead end-to-end design for key initiatives within our UK and international experiences, as well as our post purchase experiences globally, across App and Web. You’ll be driving from discovery through to delivery and iteration—achieving meaningful customer and business outcomes.

•
Own complex flows and ambiguous problem spaces, defining clear problem statements, success metrics, and design direction.

•
Partner closely with product, engineering, and data to make informed trade-offs and deliver intuitive, high-quality experiences.

•
Balance speed and quality, making pragmatic decisions while contributing to a cohesive product experience.

•
Use research, data, and experimentation to inform decisions and continuously improve outcomes.

•
Contribute to design systems and patterns, strengthening consistency and scalability across your area.

•
Facilitate alignment and decision-making, ensuring teams move forward with clarity.

•
Support and mentor other designers, helping raise the quality of work across the team.

What we look for

•
Strong Craft & Execution: You consistently deliver polished, thoughtful interaction and visual design with high attention to detail.

•
Product Thinking: You balance user needs, business goals, and technical constraints to make sound design decisions and improve end-to-end experiences.

•
Ownership & Initiative: You take ownership of ambiguous problems and drive work forward with minimal oversight.

•
Cross-functional Collaboration: You build strong partnerships, communicate clearly, and help teams align on decisions and trade-offs.

•
Data-Informed Decision Making: You use research, experimentation, and analytics to guide your work and iterate toward better outcomes.

•
Team-Level Influence: You’re a trusted design partner within your area, contributing to direction and improving how the team works.

•
Growth & Adaptability: You seek feedback, continuously improve your craft, and leverage modern tools—including AI—to accelerate your workflow.

•
Tools & Experience: Proficiency with modern design and collaboration tools (Figma, G Suite, Notion, etc.).

•
5+ years of product design experience or equivalent practical experience.

Why You'll Love Working Here

•
You’ll design financial products that genuinely help people.

•
You’ll work on high-impact experiences used by millions of customers.

•
You’ll join a team that values craft, collaboration, and thoughtful iteration.

•
You’ll have the opportunity to grow your scope, influence, and leadership over time.

This is a remote-first position based in the UK with the option to work from our London office for candidates who prefer an office environment.

Compensation & Benefits

Base Pay Grade: L

Equity Grade: UK 5

Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure based on a variety of factors, including location, experience, and job-related skills.

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness, and tech spending, and benefits including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental, and vision for you and your dependents. In addition, employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc.

GBR base pay range per year: £101,000 - 149,000

Location: Remote UK

Remote-first with flexibility built inAffirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.

Benefits designed for youOur benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:

• Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.

• Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.

• Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.

• Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.

We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help.

For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law.

title: Senior UI / UX Designer
description:
Astrid is a gaming studio that brings together accomplished world builders and game developers to create multiplayer creative experiences. Our first project is a cooperative open-world sim, designed to foster connection, problem-solving and shared discovery. Players embark on a profound social experience in a richly imagined world shaped by dynamic systems, immersive storytelling and community-driven play.

Our team spans the US, the UK and beyond. We are taking a fully remote approach, but have regular in-person meetups to synchronize, huddle and build our culture.

We are currently seeking a Senior UI/UX Designer to become a vital part of our team. A huge amount of this game lives in its UI - inventory, crafting, building, decorating and dialogue - alongside the tools and items players use to explore the world, solve problems and meet the creatures in it. You will own that player-facing experience end to end, working closely with a UI engineer and guiding outsourced graphic designers.

WHO YOU ARE

Above all, we’re looking for someone with solid gaming experience who cares about UX - not just how things look, but how they work and how they feel. The brief is broad appeal, but with layers of optional depth: a low floor and a high ceiling, where the floor stays low as the ceiling rises. It’s easy to allow the depth for advanced players to complicate things for everyone; we want the opposite, complexity players discover and opt into rather than have forced upon them. Simple shouldn’t mean sterile, though: we love the small animations and satisfying feedback that give a UI charm, the Nintendo-like sense of play that makes it a pleasure to use.

If you can make something rich for experts, welcoming to newcomers and a joy to use, you’re who we’re looking for.

In order of priority, the skills we're looking for are:

• UX - Making the game simple to pick up but deep to master. This matters most, by a clear margin

• Unreal (UMG) - Able to implement your own designs in-engine, working alongside a UI engineer

• Graphic Design - A strong visual sense is a bonus rather than a requirement

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Own the UX across the game's core systems: flows, information architecture, interaction and layout

• Design the HUD, menus, screens and moment-to-moment input so they read clearly and feel great to use

• Produce wireframes, prototypes and mock-ups and take them through to final implementation

• Build and wire up your UI in Unreal (UMG), working alongside a UI engineer

• Define and maintain a UI design system that the team and external vendors can build to

• Direct outsourced graphic designers on iconography, colour and visual polish

• Run playtests and iterate quickly as the game evolves

Requirements

• 5+ years designing UI/UX for games, with at least one shipped title or substantial in-development work

• A strong portfolio of UI/UX work on systems-rich games that shows your process and thinking

• Proven ability to make complex systems simple and intuitive without flattening their depth

• Demonstrable understanding of cosy / life-sim / management games and adventure games, since you'll be designing a hybrid of the two

• Hands-on experience building UI in Unreal (UMG). We'll consider an exceptional UX candidate with lighter Unreal, but some practical experience here is strongly expected

• Fluency with Figma and / or Adobe Suite

Benefits

• Great compensation package and equity

• Private health insurance

• Pension

• Unlimited vacation days. We trust our team!

• Flexible remote work hours as long as team members deliver results

• We are committed to continuing to expand our benefits and perks to support our team

title: Human-Centered Design Specialist IV - UI/UX
description:
Overview

LMI is seeking a Human-Centered Design (HCD) Specialist III-IV - UI/UX to support the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) portfolio. This role will focus on creating intuitive, accessible, visually cohesive, and user-centered digital experiences based on stakeholder research and user needs.

The successful candidate will bring a strong background in user experience and user interface design, with demonstrated ability to translate research findings, workflows, and requirements into high-quality digital experiences. This individual will create user flows, wireframes, prototypes, interaction patterns, interface designs, and reusable design components that guide development teams from concept through implementation.

The role will work across the HCD lifecycle, including discovery, stakeholder engagement, design, prototyping, usability testing, and iteration. Compared with a technically oriented HCD role, this position will place greater emphasis on interaction design, visual hierarchy, interface behavior, usability, design systems, and the quality and consistency of the overall user experience.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

UI/UX and Product Design

• Design intuitive, effective, and visually cohesive user experiences for digital products supporting VA programs and stakeholders.

• Translate research findings, business requirements, user needs, and technical requirements into clear design concepts.

• Develop user flows, task flows, information architectures, navigation models, wireframes, interface designs, and interactive prototypes.

• Create low- through high-fidelity designs that enable stakeholders to experience and evaluate concepts before development.

• Design interface components, interaction patterns, layouts, forms, dashboards, workflows, and data-rich experiences.

• Establish and apply consistent visual and interaction patterns across digital products.

• Contribute to design systems, component libraries, UX standards, and reusable design assets where appropriate.

• Prepare clear developer handoff documentation and collaborate with technical teams during implementation.

• Participate in design reviews and provide design guidance as solutions move from prototype through development.

HCD Research and Discovery

• Conduct stakeholder interviews, user interviews, workshops, usability studies, and other HCD discovery activities.

• Help stakeholders articulate user goals, needs, frustrations, behaviors, workflows, and desired outcomes.

• Synthesize qualitative research into findings, themes, personas, user journeys, experience maps, design principles, and recommendations.

• Connect research findings directly to UI/UX design decisions.

• Develop and test design hypotheses through prototypes and iterative user feedback.

• Facilitate usability testing and translate test results into prioritized design improvements.

Accessibility and Inclusive Design

• Apply Section 508, WCAG, and inclusive-design requirements to digital experiences.

• Design for users with different abilities, levels of digital proficiency, roles, and operating environments.

• Incorporate accessibility considerations into navigation, forms, visual hierarchy, content presentation, interaction patterns, and prototypes.

• Collaborate with technical teams to address accessibility early rather than treating compliance as a final-stage review.

Magnify Reports and HCD Deliverables

• Support development of Magnify Reports, the formal HCD deliverable associated with each SBIR contract.

• Provide research findings, personas, journey maps, visualizations, prototype concepts, user feedback, and design recommendations for inclusion in formal HCD documentation.

• Develop polished visual artifacts and presentations to communicate findings and proposed experiences to client and internal stakeholders.

• Clearly document design rationale and trace significant design decisions back to user research or validated requirements.

Stakeholder and Team Collaboration

• Facilitate design sessions, co-design workshops, prototype reviews, and usability-testing sessions.

• Present design concepts and explain design decisions to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Collaborate closely with HCD researchers, technical designers, developers, analysts, product owners, healthcare subject matter experts, and program leadership.

• Balance user needs, business requirements, accessibility considerations, and technical constraints when developing solutions.

• Participate in Agile ceremonies and integrate UX activities into iterative delivery cycles.

• Participate actively in LMI's HCD community of practice by sharing tools, templates, patterns, techniques, and lessons learned.

Qualifications

Required

• Bachelor's degree in Human-Centered Design, User Experience Design, Interaction Design, Graphic Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Information Design, Psychology, or a related field.

• 5-7+ years of professional experience in UI/UX, product design, HCD, interaction design, or a related discipline.

• Demonstrated experience designing digital products from early concept through prototype and development handoff.

• Strong proficiency with Figma or comparable modern UI/UX design and prototyping tools.

• Demonstrated experience developing user flows, wireframes, interactive prototypes, and polished interface designs.

• Strong understanding of information architecture, interaction design, visual hierarchy, usability, and user-centered design principles.

• Experience conducting or participating in user research and usability testing.

• Ability to translate research findings and complex requirements into intuitive user experiences.

• Knowledge of Section 508, WCAG, accessibility, and inclusive-design practices.

• Strong written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills.

• Ability to independently organize and prioritize design work across multiple activities.

• Ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance.

Desired

• Master's degree in Human-Centered Design, Human-Computer Interaction, UX Design, Interaction Design, or a related field.

• Portfolio demonstrating UI/UX design, research-informed design decisions, user flows, wireframes, prototypes, design systems, or shipped digital experiences.

• Experience designing for federal government, healthcare, public-sector, or enterprise environments.

• Prior experience supporting VA or VHA programs.

• Experience designing dashboards, complex workflows, enterprise applications, or data-rich experiences.

• Experience creating or contributing to design systems and reusable component libraries.

• Familiarity with Microsoft Power Platform, SharePoint, Power BI, or Microsoft 365 environments.

• Experience with Agile, Lean UX, Design Thinking, or iterative product development.

• Relevant UX, accessibility, HCD, or Agile certifications.

Target salary range: $100,000 - $130,000.

Individual salaries are determined by various factors including, but not limited to location, internal equity, business considerations, client contract requirements, and candidate qualifications, such as education, experience, skills, and security clearances.

title: Senior Product Design Strategist
description:
Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.

Job overview:

A Product + Design Strategist can carry a problem from an ambiguous user and business opportunity to a validated experience. As a Product + Design Strategist, you will operate at a senior IC level: leading the highest-leverage, most ambiguous scopes of work at Omada and setting direction for a collection of related experiences rather than a single feature. You translate engineering’s increased pace into more of the right experiences launched for our customers and members, not just more output.

AI is a core part of how this role works day to day as a co-intelligent partner you direct across research synthesis, prototyping, spec drafting, and analysis, extending your judgment so you can move from open question to validated direction faster, with more rigor.

You thrive in ambiguity, especially in 0 to 1 spaces where the problem is not yet defined and the path forward is yours to shape. You bring a strong, evidence-backed point of view, initiative and ability to find answers, and you're as comfortable in an executive strategy conversation as you are prototyping with users.

Core Responsibilities

A Product + Design Strategist owns four things — problem framing, direction setting, vision casting, and alignment. Everything else is craft in service of these.

Problem framing — turning ambiguous asks, business opportunities, and lived member experience into a scoped, evidence-backed understanding of what's actually wrong and worth solving.

• Problem framing & requirements — turning a vague ask into a scoped, buildable piece of work.

• User journey mapping — diagnosing end-to-end friction and drop-off with empathy.

• Research study design & execution — running interviews, surveys, and experiments to test assumptions.

• Data analysis (quant + qual) — pulling product performance data and synthesizing qualitative signal into a clear read of the problem.

• Competitive, inspiration, & analogous research — auditing adjacent products for pattern or gap insight.

• Metrics instrumentation — in partnership with data analytics, defining upfront what “solved” will actually look like.

Direction setting — reconciling research, data, engineering, and business input into a clear point of view on what to pursue, and revisiting that call against real evidence once it's live.

• Synthesis & direction-setting — recommending which directions to pursue and which to drop.

• Prioritization & trade-offs — arbitrating competing product and stakeholder requests with transparent rationale.

• Quantitative and qualitative evaluation design & analysis — defining core questions and hypotheses, then translating results into insights and go/no-go decisions.

• Stop/start/continue investment decisions — revisiting prior bets against evidence of what's actually working.

• Vendor & partner evaluations — build vs. buy justifications.

Vision casting — making the future state tangible and compelling enough that cross-functional partners, leadership, and members can see it and support it.

• Roadmap ownership & narrative — owning a multi-quarter roadmap that maps to corporate OKRs, key strategic initiatives, operational cadences, and commercial cycles.

• Executive communications & narratives — building the strategic story for budget and prioritization conversations.

• Product marketing & commercial partnerships — carrying the vision into go-to-market and partner contexts.

• Visual & interaction design — makes the vision tangible enough to inform viability, desirability, and feasibility decisions, and to support build and operational planning. Brings strong product taste, and can articulate what makes a health experience good in both strategic and tangible terms.

• Prototyping — building click-through and interactive prototypes to test and communicate ideas.

Alignment — keeping every function that touches the work — engineering, clinical, ops, leadership — moving on the same understanding of what's being built and why.

• Stakeholder syncs & demos — running team meetings, reviews, and critiques that keep work visible.

• Cross-functional handoff — prepping documents and prototypes that give build and operations teams clarity.

• Clinical, legal, and regulatory partnerships — integrating guidance on safety, quality, and compliance throughout.

• Launch & release readiness — owning the go/no-go call and sequencing logic for a release, in partnership with Product Ops, who runs the operational checklist and cross-team chase.

• Stakeholder alignment on product priorities and vision — resolving cross-functional disagreement directly.

Core Skills

Product + Design Strategists are T-shaped: every Strategist can operate across all of this at a working level, and leans deeper into a Design, PM, research, and/or operational specialty depending on the scope they're leading. The craft toolkit a Product + Design Strategist draws on includes:

• Prototyping — low- to high-fidelity mockups and click-through flows to test and communicate ideas, including coded experiences that give users and stakeholders a more immersive way to test.

• Visual & interaction design — applying design system components, typography, and interaction patterns to real screens and other touchpoints; drafting microcopy and in-product messaging.

• Writing PRDs/specs — documenting functional requirements and success metrics for engineering handoff.

• Backlog grooming & sprint planning — writing and prioritizing tickets, estimating scope with engineering.

• Product/design/research documentation — maintaining decision logs and research repositories so knowledge supports entire teams.

• Accessibility & QA review — checking designs and built product against accessibility standards.

• AI orchestration & prompting fluency — directing AI tools effectively across design, spec, and analysis work.

• Data-informed strategy — interpreting quantitative and qualitative data, such as product analytics and clinical outcomes, to inform product strategy and build.

• Facilitation — running workshops, critiques, and cross-functional working sessions in service of decisionmaking and alignment.

• Engineering/technical literacy — enough fluency to reason about feasibility and scope trade-offs in partnership with Eng and Ops.

We'd love to talk more if you have…

• 8+ years of experience solving complex, ambiguous problems across product management, design, and/or research, including a track record of owning outcomes at a multi-team level.

• 3-5 years of demonstrated success carrying work from 0 to 1 — defining new products or experiences from an undefined problem space through to a shipped, measurable result.

• A strong, evidence-based point of view, with the judgment to reconcile research, data, engineering, and business input into a clear direction — and the conviction to defend it and the humility to revise it.

• 3-5 years of experience owning a multi-quarter roadmap and communicating it persuasively to executive and cross-functional audiences, including budget and prioritization conversations.

• High craft in at least 2 specialist areas (design, product management, strategy, research, or operations), with genuine working fluency across the others.

• Excellence in prototyping, and fluency with modern AI-assisted prototyping and building tools (e.g., Claude Code, Claude Design, Figma Make, Cursor, Lovable, or similar) — this is a required, hands-on craft skill for this role, not a nice-to-have.

• Experience partnering with clinical, legal, regulatory, or other high-stakes compliance functions in health, wellness, fintech, or another regulated domain.

• Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with a 3-5 year track record of influencing decisions across senior leadership.

• Experience mentoring or informally leading other ICs, even without formal people-management responsibility.

• Fluency with AI orchestration and prompting across design, spec, and analysis work, and comfort pulling data directly from self-serve analytics tools.

Bonus points if you have…

• Experience designing or leading strategy for clinical, care delivery, or chronic condition management experiences.

• Experience building production-adjacent or fully coded prototypes.

• A background as a specialist in 2 areas (Design, PM, or Research) who has deliberately broadened into other health or technology disciplines rather than staying siloed.

• Experience in a startup setting, operating like a builder — self-driven, biased toward action, and energized by owning problems from discovery through launch.

• Experience running vendor and partner evaluations, including build-vs-buy business cases.

What this role is not:

To protect focus, Product + Design Strategists are not expected to own all day-to-day project coordination and status reporting (Product Ops and automated tooling own the checklist and cross-team chase once you've made the go/no-go call), detailed design of every screen and flow (owned by UX Design and Engineering, enabled by design-system-aware prototyping and coding tools), high-volume or specialized content production (owned by the content platform team), or administrative backlog upkeep (AI-assisted or Eng-owned). Formal people management of other Strategists sits with Product + Design Directors; Strategists at this level lead through influence, craft, and mentorship rather than direct reports.

Our Design Roots

Omada was founded in 2011 out of IDEO, where our founders explored how human-centered design could be applied to chronic health challenges. What began as an internal project grounded in deep user research evolved into a new approach to digital care.

That origin continues to shape how we work today. We place a strong emphasis on understanding real human needs, designing from first principles, and creating experiences that are not only effective, but engaging and thoughtfully crafted.

Design is not a layer at Omada. It is foundational to how we build products, make decisions, and deliver care.

Benefits:

• Competitive salary with generous annual cash bonus

• Equity grants

• Employee stock purchasing plan (ESPP)

• Remote first work from home culture

• Flexible Time Off to help you rest, recharge, and connect with loved ones

• Generous parental leave

• Health, dental, and vision insurance (and above market employer contributions)

• 401k retirement savings plan

• Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA)

• Mental Health Support Solutions

• ...and more!

It takes a village to change health care. As we build together toward our mission, we strive to embody the following values in our day-to-day work. We hope these hold meaning for you as well as you consider Omada!

•
Cultivate Trust. We listen closely and we operate with kindness. We provide respectful and candid feedback to each other.

•
Seek Context. We ask to understand and we build connections. We do our research up front to move faster down the road.

•
Act Boldly. We innovate daily to solve problems, improve processes, and find new opportunities for our members and customers.

•
Deliver Results. We reward impact above output. We set a high bar, we’re not afraid to fail, and we take pride in our work.

•
Succeed Together. We prioritize Omada’s progress above team or individual. We have fun as we get stuff done, and we celebrate together.

•
Remember Why We’re Here. We push through the challenges of changing health care because we know the destination is worth it.

About Omada Health: Omada Health (Nasdaq: OMDA) is reverse engineering the way healthcare is delivered in America, putting the space between doctor visits–where health is won or lost–at the center of care. Today's healthcare system poorly serves chronic conditions that require ongoing support outside of the exam room, like obesity, diabetes, hypertension, cholesterol, and musculoskeletal conditions. Omada’s virtual-first model combines human-led care teams, connected devices, and AI-enabled technology to deliver personalized care at scale, including support for GLP-1 therapy. Omada has served more than two million members since launch across 2,000+ employers, health plans, pharmacy benefit managers, and health systems. Learn more at omadahealth.com.

Wayfinder is the third organization to join the Lemnis Collective. The Collective brings mission-aligned organizations (both for-profit assets and nonprofits with earned revenue) under the Lemnis umbrella through mergers and acquisitions. Lemnis provides long-term, mission-driven investment, stability, freedom from the pressure of constant fundraising, and operational and strategic support, so organizations like Wayfinder can stay focused on our mission, impact, growth, and innovation.

What We Value

You’ll be joining a team of incredibly motivated and dedicated staff members committed to living our organization's values. We work collaboratively across teams, and we feel and act like a purpose-driven organization. To the best of our abilities, each person’s role aligns with their own sense of purpose, which feeds into Wayfinder’s larger sense of purpose.

Read this article about our workplace culture in Conscious Company.

We value equal access, inclusive community, and belonging, and these values are represented in our product, our team, and our school partners.

Product: We develop our learning tools using human-centered design principles. We work with grade-level experts to ensure our curriculum is developmentally appropriate and engaging at all levels. Every Wayfinder lesson is supported by relevant research, prototyped in classrooms, and vetted by teachers over rounds of feedback and iteration. We use Universal Design for Learning principles to give every student an equal opportunity to succeed.

Team: Our team is composed of people from all different backgrounds and walks of life. We intentionally recruit, hire, and work with people of all identities + experiences. We focus on belonging: being connected, accepted, and valued by the people around us.

School Partners: We intentionally target a wide array of educational partners, from traditional to non-traditional, that work with a range of students from different socioeconomic groups. We’ve taught our curriculum in high-need schools in the Bronx, independent schools in Silicon Valley, and after-school programs in San Antonio.

The Role

At Wayfinder, we believe every student deserves to develop belonging, purpose, and future-ready skills. Our web platform is where that happens every day for students, educators, and school communities, and we're looking for a Senior Product Designer to help shape what it becomes next.

You'll own the design of a set of features, from the first conversation with an educator to the final handoff to engineering. That means spending real time with the people who use our product. You'll talk with teachers, school leaders, and Wayfinder staff, watch how they work, and bring what you learn back to the team. Then you'll turn it into experiences that feel simple, thoughtful, and genuinely useful.

This role is for someone who's energized by understanding people's problems, loves collaborating to solve them, and is excited about the ways AI is changing both how we design and what we can build. You'll report to our Principal Product Designer and join a small team where your work has a direct, visible impact.

We strongly encourage people from traditionally underrepresented populations in tech - such as women, People of Color, People with Disabilities, and LGBTQ+ people, etc - to apply!

Responsibilities

•
Own the end-to-end design of a set of features, from discovery and research through concepting, prototyping, and handoff.

•
Lead research for your features: plan and run interviews, usability studies, and conversations with educators and students, and use product analytics to fill in the picture.

•
Get out and talk to people. Build relationships with current partners, listen closely, and bring their needs, frustrations, and ideas into the design process.

•
Share what you learn clearly and often, through written summaries, presentations, and prototypes that help the team make good decisions.

•
Translate concepts and technical requirements into sketches, user flows, prototypes, and handoff-ready files that balance a great user experience with business goals.

•
Design interfaces that are intuitive and accessible to all learners, aligned with our brand guidelines, design system, and patterns.

•
Design AI-enabled features that make work easier for educators and learning more meaningful for students, and use AI tools to speed up and strengthen your own design process.

•
Work closely with educators, designers, and engineers from discovery to delivery.

•
Turn your designs into build-ready specs and tickets so engineering can move quickly and confidently.

•
Contribute to the maintenance and growth of our component library.

Requirements

Essential experience

•
5+ years of experience in UI and UX design, with a portfolio of case studies that shows your process as well as your results.

•
A track record of leading design research, such as interviews, usability studies, and engagement with partners or customers, and turning findings into clear design decisions.

•
Excellent communication skills. You're comfortable leading a conversation with a teacher, presenting to stakeholders, and explaining your thinking in writing, sketches, and prototypes.

•
Experience designing accessible products and a working knowledge of accessibility standards (such as WCAG).

•
Comfort using AI tools as part of your design workflow, and curiosity about designing AI-enabled experiences.

•
Proficiency with Figma and familiarity with Adobe tools.

•
Experience collaborating with designers and engineers to create coherent, intuitive user experiences.

•
The ability to own your work independently, manage your own priorities in a fast-moving environment, and welcome feedback as part of doing your best work.

•
An entrepreneurial mindset and a bias toward action.

•
Fluency in written and spoken English.

Preferred experience

•
Experience designing PreK-12 edtech products, especially in Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS), college and career readiness (CCR), or durable skill development.

•
Experience designing AI-enabled features or workflows.

•
Experience working in a startup or other fast-moving environment.

•
An undergraduate degree or equivalent experience in product design, interaction design, human-computer interaction, software engineering, or a related field.

Benefits

We offer a competitive package that is based on location and experience. We also offer the following benefits:

•
+ 403b: We care about your ability to save for your future.

•
+ Family Focus: Parental leave and flexibility for families.

•
+ Time Off: Unlimited PTO policy to encourage people to get out and see the world.

•
+ Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision policies + a monthly wellness stipend.

•
+ Goodies: Whatever hardware and software you need to get the job done.

•
+ Team Fun: Regularly scheduled events, annual retreat, and celebrations.

•
+ Learning: Learning & Development Opportunities to grow your skills and career.

•
+ Great team: Working with fun, hard-working, kind people committed to making a difference!

•
+ Flexible culture: We are results-focused and entirely remote.

•
+ And much more! Lots of other perks make this company an incredible place to work.

Location

Remote work. Wayfinders’ regular operating hours are Monday-Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The daily work schedule may vary depending on the crew in which you are working.

Next Steps, If Interested

If you are interested, please fill out the job application here.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

EEO Statement

At Wayfinder, we don’t just accept differences — we celebrate them, we support them, and we thrive on them for the benefit of our employees, our products, and our community. Wayfinder is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Pay Transparency

Wayfinder compensation is based on various factors including but not limited to job location, a candidate's education, training, experience, expected quality and quantity of work, required travel (if any), external market and internal value analysis including seniority and merit systems, as well as internal pay alignment. Annual salary is just one component of Wayfinder’s total compensation package. Additionally, Wayfinder provides a variety of benefits to employees, including health insurance coverage, a monthly stipend, office buildout stipend, a retirement savings plan, paid holidays and paid time off. Compensation ranges may differ based on contract value but will be commensurate with job duties and relevant work experience. An applicant's salary history will not be used in determining compensation.

Reasonable Accommodations

Wayfinder is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation, contact HR at .

Additional Notice

Please note that this job description is only a summary of the typical functions of the job, not an exhaustive or comprehensive list of all possible responsibilities, tasks, and duties.

We are open to candidates based in the Americas.

We believe magic happens when thoughtful collaboration and unparalleled expertise come together to turn great ideas into great products. Design Leads at Metalab play a direct role in that magic. They steer projects in the right direction by leading the day-to-day work internally and managing clients' expectations, while also getting into the files themselves. It’s about high-quality output and outcomes.

As a Design Lead, you’ll have a vested interest in helping other designers find their groove. Given that our primary focus is product design, a deep understanding of what it takes to get digital products out the door is our first non-negotiable. Beyond that, you’ve established yourself as someone people look up to, and you don’t take that privilege lightly. You’ll still deal in pixels, but you’ll also play an integral role in a project’s success with clear direction, leadership, guidance, and encouragement. You believe that good ideas can come from anywhere, and you actively support your team in making sure everyone is heard.

What you’ll do

• Guide the design process throughout the entire project lifecycle

• Drive client presentations and discussions of your team’s work

• Respectfully decline the status quo and push both clients and colleagues outside their comfort zones

• Foster positive client relationships and directly influence client stakeholders

• Work with Product Managers and Client Partners to scope project requirements

• Help promote an inspiring and inclusive environment for the team

• Coach and mentor Product Designers to determine and work towards desired career growth paths, sharing tailored feedback and guidance, and monitoring overall fulfillment and happiness

• Work hand-in-hand with engineers and product team members to foster innovation and ensure feasibility and fidelity of implementation

• Promote a culture of autonomy balanced with proven ways of working

Requirements

• 5+ years of product design experience at a digital product agency or consultancy, ideally in a Lead role

• Demonstrated mastery of UI/UX principles, best practices, and common design tools (read: Figma)

• Adequate level of interaction design skills to guide the work (think After Effects, Principle, Framer, Origami)

• A portfolio that reflects your strengths in UX and visual design

• A natural inclination to take the lead and help everyone arrive at a deeper understanding and greater appreciation of the work

• Fluent in translating stakeholder goals, user research, and complex user flows into simple UIs

• Passionate about staying ahead of desktop and mobile best practices, developments, and trends in web, mobile, and iOS design

• Communication pro, with the ability to deliver compelling design rationales in both client and internal contexts

• Comfortable with ambiguity and client briefs that lead to more questions than answers

• Motivated by feedback, and by the opportunity to improve in your role, in the work, and in how you work together as a team

Equal opportunity employer

Research shows that women and other marginalized groups tend to only apply for a job when they meet every single criteria. Does this role sound like it was made for you, yet you don’t check every box? Reach out anyways! We’re an equal opportunity employer and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and diverse environment for employees from all walks of life. We hire based on talent, and we’re proud of our global perspective.

User Experience & Interface Design

Design and iterate on user-centered experiences that improve navigation, usability, and accessibility across our web and mobile platforms.

Develop high-fidelity UI designs and interactive prototypes to effectively communicate design solutions to the team and stakeholders.

description:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.

We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.

We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.

About the Role

Location: Remote (United States, Europe, Canada, or LATAM)

Role Type: Full-time

Reporting to: VP of Engineering

Compensation: $148,000 to $190,000 per year for US-based applicants. Adjusted contingent on location for applicants based in Canada, LATAM, and Europe.

CodePath's educational programs run on our learning platform, a set of applications with functionality spanning admissions, course delivery, grading, career coaching, and reporting. These tools have been amazingly effective, but we’re increasingly seeing our limited design bandwidth holding us back in our efforts to take them further.

We're looking for our first Senior Product Designer to own the experience design of the platform: how a flow is structured, how people navigate, how an interaction feels. You'll also own the design system that keeps everything coherent as the platform grows.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You'll own the work end to end: talk to the people who use our products, decide how an experience should work, and hand engineers something they can build from.

We focus on what's most impactful for our students: the quality of the experience. A UI-focused contractor is available to you as a resource, and you'll set the direction they execute against.

The ideal candidate is a designer inspired by potential projects like these:

• Designing the Learner Hub, the student-facing part of our Career Mobility OS: personalized career roadmaps, skills tracking, and employer-connected pathways

• Building and owning CodePath's first design system: its interaction patterns and components

• Untangling and redesigning the core platform areas no single product manager owns today, like accounts, onboarding, and navigation

• Designing the interfaces for AI-powered learning tools, including tutoring, coaching, and grading

Key Activities

• Design end-to-end user flows, navigation, and information architecture across the platform, and document them as wireframes and specifications engineers can build from

• Own CodePath's design system: the interaction patterns, components, and standards that keep the platform consistent

• Run lightweight product discovery. Talk to students, staff, and internal stakeholders to define what's needed, especially for platform areas and internal tools that no product manager owns

• Partner with product managers to turn prioritized initiatives into build-ready designs, and with engineers to resolve design questions as they build

• Direct a UI design contractor to extend your output

• Set and hold the bar for experience quality across the product

Qualifications

• 6+ years designing web products end-to-end, with a portfolio that shows your thinking on flows and structure and the process behind your work

• Strong information architecture and interaction design skills. You can take an ambiguous problem and produce a clear flow, navigation model, and spec

• Experience running your own discovery: talking to users and stakeholders to figure out what's needed rather than waiting for a fully specified brief

• Experience building a design system

• Fluency producing engineer-ready artifacts (wireframes, prototypes, specs) in Figma or a comparable tool

•
Comfort with ambiguity and small-team dynamics. You've worked without a large design org around you and know how to prioritize without perfect information
