title: Product Designer (UX), HCI
description:
About ActAI

here are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations.

Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things.

Role

Design how people use AI in real product workflows. This role focuses on building HCI interfaces where users can understand, guide, correct, and stay in control of AI systems that reason and act across multiple steps.

Current UX patterns are not enough for proactive AI products. You will help define new interaction models for how users work with AI, review progress, recover from mistakes, and build trust in the system.

What You'll Be Doing

•
Design end-to-end user experiences for AI product surfaces, from concept to shipped product.

•
Create interaction patterns for human-AI workflows, including prompting, review, confirmation, correction, handoff, and recovery.

•
Design interfaces that help users understand what the AI is doing, what it knows, what it is unsure about, and what will happen next.

•
Turn complex, multi-step AI capabilities into flows that are clear, controllable, and usable in everyday contexts.

•
Work closely with product, engineering, and ML teams to define problems, test ideas, and ship quickly.

•
Produce wireframes, flows, prototypes, and high-fidelity designs for web and mobile.

•
Run lightweight user research and usability tests to identify friction, trust issues, and failure points.

•
Help define reusable HCI design patterns as the product and design system mature.

What You Will Need

•
Experience as a product designer or UX designer, with a portfolio across web or mobile products.

•
Strong skills in interaction design, information hierarchy, and prototyping.

•
Proficiency in Figma and fast iteration workflows.

•
Ability to simplify complex systems and turn unclear product behavior into clear user experiences.

•
Experience working closely with product managers and engineers in fast-moving teams.

•
Comfort working with ambiguity and shaping solutions before requirements are fully defined.

•
Good judgment on usability, edge cases, and failure handling.

•
Clear thinking about trust, control, feedback, and transparency in AI-driven experiences.

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2 rounds of interviews and a design assessment.

Applications are evaluated by our team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us. title: Senior Product Designer
description:
Fully Remote (UK based) | Competitive Salary + Bonus + Generous Equity | B Corp Certified
TrustedHousesitters is a fast growing, direct-to-consumer marketplace that is redefining pet care and travel.

Here at TrustedHousesitters, we’re on a mission to make travel work better for pets, for their people, and for the global community of animal lovers who look after them. We’ve got big plans on becoming the world’s most-loved travel solution for pet people. We’ve built something pretty special: a trusted place where pet owners and sitters connect to keep pets happy at home while their humans explore the world.

We’ve already grown into a global community with members in over 140 countries, a product people genuinely love, and a team of more than 100 brilliant humans powering it all.

But we’re only just getting started. Our goal? To grow to 1 million members and make TrustedHousesitters the world’s most-loved travel solution for pet people.

At the moment, a sit starts every two minutes somewhere on the planet. We want that to be every single minute and we know the only way we’ll get there is with the right people in the right roles.

The right people in the right roles will shape our future. So, here’s the big question: Could that be you?

The role

We're looking for a Senior Product Designer to shape the core experience our members rely on every day across iOS, Android and web.

You'll own the moments that matter: onboarding, listing homes, finding and applying for sits, matching with the right sitter or owner, preparing for a stay. This is a hands-on role as the primary designer in your squad. You'll have real strategic influence over your area's direction and drive measurable impact for both our members and the business.

What You'll Do

• Design mobile-first experiences that work across iOS, Android and web, respecting platform conventions while staying consistent with our design system

• Own discovery research and testing for your squad (interviews, usability testing, concept testing) and measure impact using product analytics and qualitative signals to guide iteration

• Define problems and hypotheses with your squad, choose the right validation method to make sure we're building the right thing for our customers

• Design AI-powered features for matching, personalisation and communication with trust and transparency built in, and use AI tools daily to speed up exploration, prototyping and synthesis

• Work with stakeholders across product, engineering, user research, content, data and commercial teams, communicating design rationale clearly to stakeholders, facilitating workshops to create alignment and negotiating trade offs

• Contribute to and evolve the design system, partnering with Design Systems to create robust, accessible, cross-platform patterns

• Build solutions that scale. Map journeys and service relationships rather than solving problems in isolation, and champion craft and accessibility throughout

What you'll need

Strategy and systems thinking

Strong systems thinking with experience designing complex customer journeys end to end. Proven ability to set customer-centric vision and translate it into practical, phased delivery while balancing member needs with business goals and technical constraints.

Research and methodology

Hands-on user research skills, confident choosing methods and synthesising insight into clear design direction. Able to frame complex challenges into clear problem statements and testable hypotheses, with solid understanding of experimentation methods and when to use each.

Craft and execution

Exceptional interaction and visual design craft with meticulous attention to detail, including advanced prototyping and working within mature design systems. Deep knowledge of mobile interface guidelines and best practices, backed by a portfolio showing end-to-end, beautifully crafted, user-centred work with measurable impact on customer and business outcomes.

AI in design

Confident daily use of AI-assisted design and prototyping tools as part of your everyday workflow. You'll ideally be working in Cursor, Claude Code or similar for at least some of your workflow and you'll bring ideas of how AI tools can be used to drive efficiency and impact across the design process.

Collaboration and culture

Excellent communication and storytelling skills with comfort working in empowered, cross-functional squads. Experience in scale-ups with strong product and experimentation culture. You'll need to be confident in selling your ideas across the business, creating alignment and inspiring others.

Nice to have

• Experience designing AI/ML-powered features such as recommendations engines and LLMs with good understanding of the UX challenges they create - trust, comprehension, feedback loops, agency etc.

• Experience in two-sided marketplaces, subscription or membership businesses, or trust and safety-sensitive products.

• Self-serve analytics experience (we use Amplitude, Mode) and familiarity with research depository tools such as Dovetail, Chattermill.

Our hiring process

• Intro call with hiring manager

• Technical portfolio review with PM, Design lead and Engineering partner

• Leadership and first 90 days presentation

What you'll bring

You'll own the product design process end-to-end.

At TrustedHousesitters we start with the customer. You'll need to be able to show us how you've used quantitative and qualitative user research to inform your approach to solving product design problems.

You'll feel like a fish out of water if:

We know this isn't what you'd see in most job ads - but TrustedHousesitters isn't most companies.

Trust, transparency, and honest feedback aren't just things we say; they're genuinely how we operate, every day. So rather than leaving you guessing if things don't work out, we'd rather give you what you need to make a great decision upfront about whether this opportunity is right for you.

With that in mind, here are a few things worth considering before you hit apply:

• Your design experience is web-only - you haven't shaped native iOS or Android app experiences.

• Your background is mainly B2B, enterprise, or public sector - you're used to solving problems functionally, and this role needs you to think about design emotionally too.

• You'd rather be handed a fully-scoped brief than help define the problem yourself - you'll be the primary designer in your squad, shaping direction, not just executing someone else's spec.

• You're sceptical of AI having a genuine place in the design process, or you actively avoid using AI tools in your own workflow.

• When you disagree with a decision, you tend to raise it and step back - we need people who'll stay in the room and help find the way through.

🐾 For the love of pets

Contractors are responsible for their own taxes, insurance, equipment, and benefits.

Product Context

This engagement will primarily focus on PowerClerk®, Clean Power Research’s configurable, no-code workflow platform used by utilities and energy agencies to manage complex energy programs. PowerClerk streamlines application intake, review, approval, and ongoing program operations in a secure, enterprise-grade system.

The role may also contribute to projects across the SolarAnywhere® family of products, which support solar resource assessment, performance monitoring, and forecasting. These products serve a wide range of analytical and operational use cases, requiring clear, usable interfaces for technically complex data.

Scope of Work

• Collaborate with Product/Program Managers and Engineers to understand user problems, product requirements, and constraints, and propose appropriate design solutions

• Deliver high-quality designs for new features and refine existing experiences

• Partner closely with multidisciplinary teams on the ideation and definition of new user experiences

• Follow a user-centered design process, delivering design artifacts with an appropriate level of fidelity and detail at each stage

• Contribute to the development and maintenance of reusable design system components that support consistency, flexibility, and extensibility

• Contribute innovative ideas and deliver groundbreaking designs that shape the future of our products

• Transform complex concepts into engaging and intuitive user experiences

Who You Are

• Bachelor's degree in Product Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design or similar field

• 4+ years of experience in user experience design, with a strong emphasis on interaction design or similar role

• Portfolio demonstrating strong product thinking, including navigation, user flows, interaction design, information architecture, and information visualization

• Clean, modern design aesthetic with strong attention to detail and a passion for simplifying complex experiences

• Experience designing complex, data-centric web applications, with a strong understanding of how to make them intuitive and delightful

• Fluency in UX best practices, including user-centered design, interaction design, and information architecture, grounded in strong UX principles and techniques

• Experience building and contributing to a shared design system, including defining component architecture and variant structure

• Ability to write clear component documentation that other designers and engineers can use

• Experience collaborating with engineers to ensure designs are implemented consistently and efficiently

• Ability to translate ambiguous requirements into clear user flows, information architecture diagrams, wireframes, mockups, and prototypes

• Experience working across multiple levels of fidelity throughout the design process, from low-fidelity wireframes to pixel-perfect design specifications

• Advanced proficiency in Figma, including components, auto layout, and building and maintaining design libraries

• Strong time management skills, with the ability to prioritize and manage work independently against agreed timelines

• Experience with planning and executing lightweight, rapid, iterative usability testing is a plus

• Passion for renewables and for advancing the transition to clean energy

Additional Notes

• The role does not include people management responsibilities

• The focus is on individual contributor design work and delivery of defined project outcomes

Contract Compensation

• Contract Engagement: Approximately 5 months

• Hourly Rate: $55–$70 (flat rate)

• This engagement is structured as an independent contractor (1099) role and does not include employee benefits

How to Apply

Click the link below to submit your resume. Note that a portfolio review presentation is required to interview for this role. Please include a link to your portfolio and a cover letter detailing your interest in this position and the renewable energy space along with your resume.  Due to the large number of applicants for our positions, we regret that we can only respond to candidates who meet our requirements.

Clean Power Research provides equal opportunity for all contract engagements. All qualified individuals will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

title: Principal Product Designer, Design Systems Lead
location: New York, NY (HQ), San Francisco, CA, Remote (US)
description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less.

We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp.

This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change.

You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better.

You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it.

This role is for you if you’re excited by:

 - Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same.

 - Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality.

 - Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional.

The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead and develop the design systems team. Set clear priorities, ownership, and goals. Give direct, timely feedback, hold people accountable, and help them do the best work of their careers.

 - Own the system’s vision and direction. Decide what to preserve, evolve, simplify, or replace based on what builders and customers need. Turn that direction into focused work the team can deliver.

 - Elevate Ramp’s visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path.

 - Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference experiences, composition rules, and guidance that produce better work without you in the room.

 - Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance, compose interfaces, and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use.

 - Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, work in code, and get into implementation details to test ideas, unblock the team, and understand where the system breaks down.

 - Define and measure quality. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks. Measure whether builders can ship better work faster, with less rework—not just whether they use the tools.

 - Improve the path from idea to shipped experience. Partner with engineering and AI teams on workflows that support fast exploration, useful iteration, and appropriate production safeguards.

 - Earn adoption. Work alongside product teams, listen closely, teach through examples, and turn recurring questions and exceptions into improvements to the system.

 - Keep the team moving forward. Experiment as models and tools evolve, share what you learn, and change direction when the evidence calls for it.




WHAT YOU NEED




 - Experience leading and developing strong design or design engineering teams, with a track record of setting direction and delivering meaningful outcomes.

 - Exceptional visual and interaction design skills. Your work shows a clear point of view, attention to detail, and an ability to make complex experiences feel simple.

 - Deep systems thinking and experience building systems that other teams actually adopt. You can show how your work improved both their speed and the quality of what shipped.

 - Strong technical fluency. You can prototype and build in code, understand front-end architecture, and work through implementation tradeoffs with engineers—not just hand off specifications.

 - Active, hands-on use of AI in your design and building workflow. You understand where it helps, where it fails, and how to improve its output rather than accept it.

 - Experience turning design principles into practical guidance, reusable patterns, and quality checks that work at scale.

 - Strong product judgment and a habit of staying close to the people using what you build. You connect system decisions to real workflows and customer outcomes.

 - The ability to create clarity in ambiguity, make decisions, give difficult feedback, and maintain momentum without losing the quality bar.

 - Curiosity that borders on obsession about how AI changes software and how we build it—and the ability to ignite that curiosity in others.


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building agent-usable design guidance, generation workflows, or evaluations for design quality.

 - Experience building developer or designer tools that became part of other teams’ daily workflow.

 - Experience leading a major design-system migration or company-wide change in how teams build.

 - Experience evolving a system across platforms or connecting product and brand experiences.

 - Founder or early-stage startup experience.






BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend




UNITED STATES

 - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

 - One Medical annual membership

 - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

OTHER NOTICES

title: Senior Web Designer, Growth
description:
Fin, now part of Salesforce, is on a mission to help businesses provide perfect customer experiences.

Our AI Agent Fin is the highest-performing AI Customer Agent on the market today, enabling businesses to deliver impeccable, always-on customer support across the customer journey, from service, to sales, to ecommerce. Powered by our own AI models, Fin resolves complex customer issues end-to-end across every channel, with minimal set-up and integration. Fin can also be combined with our natively integrated Intercom help desk, giving modern support teams one single system.

Together with Salesforce, the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success, we're building the future of customer experience. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn't a buzzword, it's a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing, and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI.

Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place. Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

About this role

Our website is one of the most important ways people discover what we offer, understand our value, and decide whether to talk to Sales or start a trial. The Web Growth team owns its roadmap and continuously improves the journey from first impression through to lead capture, demo engagement, signup, and trial start.

You’ll treat the website like a product: understand user intent, find confusion and friction, form strong hypotheses, test them with users and data, and turn what you learn into better experiences.

You’ll be just as comfortable shaping the problem and influencing the roadmap as you are designing the final interaction, prototype, or page.

What you’ll be doing

• Experimentation: Designing and iterating on experiments across landing pages, pricing, signup, and conversion flows to improve engagement, conversion, qualified leads, and trial starts.

• Collaboration: Working with Growth, Self-serve, Brand, Marketing, Product, Data, Research, and Engineering to turn opportunities into clear, buildable experiences.

• Data and insight: Using user insights and funnel data to identify opportunities, define hypotheses, and measure impact.

• Product design: Applying product design thinking to comprehension, navigation, forms, interactive demos, responsiveness, and accessibility.

• Prototyping and systems: Prototyping in Figma and code, using AI tools where useful, and working within shared components and brand systems.

• Roadmap ownership: Bringing ideas to the Web Growth roadmap, not just executing briefs.

Must have experience

• Experience: 5+ years in web, product, growth, or a closely related design role, with a strong portfolio of shipped, conversion-focused work.

• Growth mindset: A track record of using design, growth frameworks, conversion rate optimisation, and funnel analysis to improve outcomes such as leads, conversion, trials, activation, or revenue.

• Experimentation: Experience designing and iterating on experiments, including A/B tests or other data-informed approaches. B2B SaaS experience is a plus.

• Craft and taste: Excellent visual and interaction design skills, with a sharp eye for typography, hierarchy, detail, and polish.

• Systems and brand: Comfortable working within an existing design system and brand, while identifying opportunities to extend and improve it.

• AI fluency: Experience using AI in your design practice, including tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Figma Make, or similar. You should be able to explain how AI has changed your workflow and what you have built or shipped with it.

• Ownership: Able to take a brief and run with it. You work independently, make good decisions, ask the right questions, and bring solutions rather than just options.

Who this role is not for

This role is not for you if:

• You only want to design campaign or marketing pages from a fixed brief. This role owns the journey from first visit through to lead, demo, signup, or trial.

• You care about visual polish but not about comprehension, navigation, forms, interactive demos, or reducing friction.

• You don’t want to work with funnel data, user research, experimentation, or the realities of implementation.

• You want to focus on brand expression without balancing it with usability, accessibility, performance, and measurable growth.

• You need a fixed roadmap and detailed requirements rather than identifying opportunities and shaping what the team should test next.

• You’re not interested in working closely with Growth, Marketing, Product, Data, Research, and Engineering to make the website perform better.

What success looks like

You’ll know you’re successful if:

• More visitors understand Fin and Intercom, find the right path for their needs, and take the next step with less friction.

• You’ve improved meaningful growth outcomes across qualified leads, demo engagement, signups, and trial starts.

• Experiments are well designed, clearly measured, and used to inform what the team does next.

• You’ve made complex product value easier to understand and act on without relying on extra explanation from Sales or Marketing.

• You’ve built strong working relationships with Growth, Marketing, Product, Engineering, Data, Research, Sales, and Customer Success.

• You’ve raised the bar for web growth design through thoughtful, high-quality experiences that people trust and want to use.

Interview process

We understand that interviewing for a new role is both time- and energy-consuming. We aim to be thorough, speedy, and transparent in our approach.

You should expect the entire process to take no more than four weeks from start to finish. You’ll meet with members of our team and have the opportunity to validate that Intercom and the role are the right fit for you.

Ready to build something great?

If you’re excited by the opportunity to help existing businesses get more value from a self-serve product, and you have the craft, curiosity, commercial thinking, and autonomy to make a real impact, we’d love to hear from you.

#LI-Hybrid

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

In the United States, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. At Fin, we want to give people what they need to do the best work of their careers. Our benefits and programs are designed to support your health and wellbeing, your family, your time away from work, and your financial future. Offerings vary by location in line with local practices and requirements. Learn more about working at Fin and the benefits we offer at fin.ai/careers. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Salesforce will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Policies

Fin has a hybrid working policy. We believe that working in person helps us stay connected, collaborate easier and create a great culture while still providing flexibility to work from home. We expect employees to be in the office at least three days per week.

We have a radically open and accepting culture at Fin. We avoid spending time on divisive subjects to foster a safe and cohesive work environment for everyone. As an organization, our policy is to not advocate on behalf of the company or our employees on any social or political topics out of our internal or external communications. We respect personal opinion and expression on these topics on personal social platforms on personal time, and do not challenge or confront anyone for their views on non-work related topics. Our goal is to focus on doing incredible work to achieve our goals and unite the company through our core values.

Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.

title: UX Designer, AI App
description:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations.

Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things.

Role

You will own the UX of ActAI's core app experience. This means designing the end-to-end flows users go through every day - how they start tasks, how they follow along as the AI works, how they stay in control, and how they recover when something goes wrong.

This is a UX role for a HCI product. You need to understand both user needs and AI system behavior well enough to design product flows that feel clear, reliable, and controllable.

What You'll Be Doing

•
Own UX for ActAI's core app surfaces across iOS, Android, and web.

•
Design complete user flows for AI-assisted tasks - from intent capture through to task completion, including handoff, progress tracking, and error recovery.

•
Design how the app surfaces what the AI is doing, what decisions it has made, and what the user needs to confirm or adjust.

•
Map and design the full range of AI states a user encounters - loading, thinking, acting, waiting, completing, stalling, failing, and recovering.

•
Work with product, engineering, and ML teams to define user requirements and translate them into concrete design solutions.

•
Conduct usability research to understand where users lose trust, feel uncertain, or disengage.

•
Produce wireframes, user flows, and high-fidelity designs that engineering can build from directly.

•
Contribute to the design system and shared UX patterns for AI app surfaces.

•
Design for both simple everyday interactions and complex multi-step AI workflows within the same product.

What You Will Need

•
Experience as a UX designer on consumer mobile or web apps, with a strong portfolio.

•
Solid skills in user flow design, wireframing, and high-fidelity prototyping in Figma.

•
Ability to design for systems that are asynchronous, non-deterministic, and context-dependent.

•
Clear thinking about user trust, control, feedback, and transparency in AI-driven product experiences.

•
Experience conducting user research and turning findings into design decisions.

•
Comfortable working in fast-moving teams with evolving product scope.

•
Ability to balance simple consumer UX with complex AI system behavior.

•
Good judgment on usability, edge cases, failure handling, and recovery flows.

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product

Interview process

For design roles, we expect candidates to submit a portfolio as part of the application process.

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2 rounds of interviews and a design assessment.

Applications are evaluated by our team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us. This isn't just a job offer; it's an invitation to be part of a team that's bringing AI to have practical benefits to billions globally.

Job Description:

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact supporting the Case Management Modernization (CMM) Program. The CMM program is an initiative to support the Administrative Office of the US Courts (AO) in developing a modern cloud-based solution to support all 204+ federal courts across the United States.

GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career. The UI/UX Human Centered Design Specialist ensures dashboards, reporting tools, predictive analytics screens, and AI/ML interfaces are intuitive, accessible, and aligned with Judiciary user workflows, supporting the CMM Data Modernization and Governance team in delivering data-driven decision-support tools in alignment with strict federal compliance requirements.

This role supports the Reporting, Analytics, and Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) deliverables by shaping user-centered visual designs for the Reporting & Analytics Capability and the Measurement Definitions and Decision-Support Package. By applying human-centered design (HCD) best practices to visualizations, navigation patterns, and decision-support experiences, this role enhances adoption and interpretability while ensuring designs meet Section 508, WCAG 2.1 AA, and federal digital service standards for accessibility, performance, and security.

The UI/UX Human Centered Design Specialist will execute the following responsibilities:

Reporting & Analytics

• Design intuitive, accessible dashboards, self-service reporting interfaces, and predictive analytics screens for the CMM Reporting & Analytics Capability, applying Human-Centered Design (HCD) and usability best practices.

• Translate UX research, personas, and journey maps into high-fidelity prototypes, wireframes, and interface design specifications for development teams.

• Partner with BI Architects, data engineers, product owners, and developers to align visual designs with data models, KPIs, and reporting requirements.

• Conduct usability testing, including heuristic evaluations, card sorting, and A/B testing, on dashboards and visualizations, and apply findings to refine designs each sprint.

• Define and maintain visualization, navigation, and interaction design standards to ensure reports and dashboards are consistent, interpretable, and support adoption.

• Design the user experience for the Measurement Definitions and Decision-Support Package, ensuring metrics and KPIs are presented in a clear, decision-ready format.

• Evaluate designs for Section 508 and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility compliance across all reporting and analytics interfaces.

• Support rapid prototyping and iterative validation of dashboard and reporting designs within Agile sprint cycles.

• Drive user adoption of dashboards and reporting tools by aligning navigation patterns and visual hierarchy with Judiciary user workflows.

• Contribute standardized UI components and templates to the shared CMM design system for reuse across reporting products.

AI/ML Capabilities

• Design intuitive, explainable interfaces for AI/ML-driven predictive analytics and decision-support features, ensuring model outputs are interpretable to end users.

• Apply HCD principles to the presentation of AI/ML model outputs, confidence indicators, and recommendations to support responsible AI adoption.

• Collaborate with AI/ML and data science teams to translate model capabilities into user-facing workflows aligned with federal responsible-AI requirements for transparency, fairness, and risk mitigation.

• Conduct usability evaluations of AI/ML interfaces and incorporate feedback into iterative design refinements.

QUALIFICATIONS

• MA/MS degree, or Bachelor's/Master's degree in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Design, or a related field, with 10+ years of general experience in information systems and 8+ years of specialized experience in UI/UX design, including 5+ years in a Human-Centered Design (HCD) role supporting enterprise or government applications.

• Experience may be considered in lieu of degree as follows: HS (16+ years), AA/AS (14+ years), BA/BS (12+ years), Doctorate Degree/Ph.D. (9+ years).

• Expertise in usability testing methodologies, such as heuristic evaluations, card sorting, and A/B testing, and proficiency in design and prototyping tools (Figma, Sketch, Axure, Storybook, or similar).

• Strong understanding of Agile/SAFe delivery, iterative design integration, and DesignOps/UX governance practices.

• Familiarity with HTML5, CSS3, and responsive UI behavior to collaborate effectively with front-end developers.

• Experience designing for federal systems, with practical knowledge of Section 508 and WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.

COMMUNICATION & ORGANIZATIONAL

• Excellent presentation and communication (oral and written) skills.

• Consultant mindset with the ability to work with high level customer stakeholders and build excellent customer relationships.

• Experience identifying and applying industry tools, solutions, methods best practices, and emerging technologies.

• Strong analytical skills and problem-solving skills with the ability to formulate and communicate recommendations for improvement.

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a team.

CERTIFICATIONS (Preferred)

• Certified Usability Analyst (CUA) or Certified HCD Professional

• SAFe Agile Practitioner (SPC or SSM)

• Section 508 Trusted Tester Certification

• UX Design or HCD Certification (NN/g, IDEO, or HFI)

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

Product Design makes up over half of our design disciplines, working in tight-knit squads alongside research, product, engineering and data to solve real customer problems at scale.

We design for the "magic moments"

We’ve built a bank that feels human, not just functional. Our product is our personality. We blend research, empathy, data and craft to turn everyday interactions into memorable experiences.

Right now, we’re growing fast and looking for passionate designers to shape Monzo’s future — and there’s a huge opportunity to make your mark.

Our Growth collective is focused on helping more people discover Monzo, understand what makes us different, and find the products that can make money work better for them.

• Acting as a role model in Design, sharing your work broadly, mentoring others, and contributing to the growth and success of the wider Design team.

• You’re comfortable using data to inform your design decisions, partnering with Data Scientists or Analysts to understand customer behaviour and measure the impact of your work.

• You can connect great customer experiences with measurable outcomes and understand how design can contribute to wider product and commercial goals.

• You’re comfortable forming hypotheses, experimenting with different approaches and adapting your thinking as you learn.

• You can balance speed and experimentation with a high bar for craft, knowing when to prototype quickly and when to invest in creating an exceptional final experience.

• You’re a natural collaborator who can bring together Product, Engineering, Data, Research and other partners around complex customer problems.

• You thrive in ambiguity and can create clarity and direction when the answer isn’t immediately obvious.

• You’re comfortable thinking beyond an individual screen or experiment, connecting work across journeys and helping shape a longer-term vision.

• You’re a role model who actively contributes to the growth of the Design team through mentoring, feedback and sharing your expertise.

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team:

Web Presence & Platform (WPP) is organized into two pillars: Platform and Presence. The Platform pillar builds internal systems, tooling, and infrastructure to support the web. The Presence pillar owns Stripe’s public-facing storytelling across stripe.com, including our homepage, product landing pages, industry and solutions pages, and other high-impact go-to-market surfaces. Together, we shape how millions of people understand what Stripe is and what it can do for them.

Designers on the Presence team work at the intersection of craft and impact—balancing clarity, polish, and systems thinking with strategic storytelling and experimentation. We collaborate closely with engineering, marketing, content, and product to deliver work that is not only beautiful, but measurably moves the business.

What you’ll do

As a Designer on the Presence team, you'll contribute to the strategy and execution of Stripe’s most visible web surfaces. You’ll design new product pages, evolve storytelling for specific industries or audiences, and refine reusable patterns that make it easier to scale exceptional work across stripe.com. This is a high-impact role for a thoughtful, collaborative designer who deeply values visual craft, user clarity, and iteration.

We’re looking for someone who’s excited to operate at the intersection of storytelling, systems, and scale—and who takes pride in the pixels. Your work will directly shape how millions of users understand Stripe, and help convert interest into action across a range of audiences—from founders to enterprise CTOs.

Responsibilities

• Design new and improved experiences across stripe.com, including product, industry, and solution landing pages

• Collaborate with engineers, PMMs, and content designers to define problems, explore solutions, and bring them to life

• Partner with other designers to maintain and evolve systems that uphold Stripe’s design standards at scale

• Balance storytelling with usability to create pages that are engaging, credible, and easy to navigate

• Use user research, user testing, and data to guide and validate your decisions

• Participate in critique and feedback sessions, contributing to the overall quality bar of the team

• Demonstrate a meticulous attention to craft—ensuring designs are not only functional, but visually excellent

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these, we encourage you to apply—even if you don’t meet every preferred qualification.

Minimum requirements

• 2–4 years of relevant design experience, ideally in web or product marketing contexts

• A strong portfolio of web design work that demonstrates exceptional visual design skills, systems thinking, and attention to detail

• Ability to independently scope and lead small to medium-sized projects

• Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset

• Fluency in layout, typography, color, hierarchy, and interaction fundamentals

• Comfortable using Figma and working in component-based systems

• Experience working on CMS-driven websites and modular systems

Preferred qualifications

• Familiarity with front-end development workflows or an ability to speak fluently with engineers

• Understanding of web performance, accessibility, and SEO best practices

• Experience designing for international audiences or multilingual websites

• Previous experience in fast-paced, cross-functional environments

How we work

We care deeply about craft—but also about moving with urgency and focus. We seek feedback early and often, because we believe design gets stronger through collaboration and iteration. We keep our users front and center—whether that’s a small business owner evaluating Stripe for the first time, or a CTO trying to understand a complex product at a glance. And we take pride in delivering work that is not only beautiful and precise, but that delivers clear, measurable impact.

We value curiosity, humility, and resilience. You’ll do well here if you love to learn, enjoy working across disciplines, and bring energy and optimism into your work.

This is a great opportunity for someone eager to grow. Designers on the Presence team have gone on to lead major product launches, shape system-wide improvements, and take on leadership roles. You'll be supported by experienced peers and have space to develop your craft, influence, and ownership over time.

Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. About the Role

You have spent 7+ years designing complex digital products, ideally including SaaS, B2B, platform, workflow-heavy or similarly sophisticated product experiences, and are ready to shape product direction, design standards and team culture across one or more product pillars.

As a lead individual contributor, you will partner deeply with product and engineering leaders, mentor other designers and help teams define and improve strategically important product experiences across the HighLevel platform. Deep fluency in design systems, accessibility standards, reusable patterns and scalable product experience decisions.

Experience influencing design direction for high-impact product areas, systems, platforms or pillars, not only individual features or flows.

Excellent communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to simplify complex ideas, lead critiques and workshops and persuade through rationale, evidence and craft.

Passion for improving team operations, design standards, processes, tools, documentation and better ways for teams to work.

description:
At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires.

What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

Quality is our competitive advantage. Every member of our fully remote team is a maker at heart, caring deeply about the quality and feel of our work. While the industry optimizes for speed and metrics alone, we believe that craft and quality have lasting value. Quality creates gravity — it pulls people toward our team and product rather than requiring us to push. This philosophy drives everything we do, from product decisions to hiring choices.

For this role, we expect robust design skills, sharp product thinking, and the ability to engage in technical discussions. We work in small, autonomous project teams, where engineers are paired tightly with designers to explore ideas, build prototypes, deploy internal builds, and ultimately ship to customers. You will be a key element of projects from beginning to end.

Location & work mode

Linear is a remote-first company, with optional co-working offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. This role is open to candidates based in North America. You can work from anywhere within this region. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel.

What you'll do

 - Own the experience of our iOS and Android mobile apps, including guiding the adaptation of desktop features to mobile

 - Pair closely with mobile engineers and product leads to initiate and complete mobile-specific projects, no hand-offs

 - Take opportunities to redesign or refine key screens and flows, as well as smaller quality issues and “paper cuts” as you use Linear

title: Product Designer
location: New York, New York, New York, United States
description:
Compensation: $160kâ190k base + meaningful equity

About Flint

The best education anyone has ever received is one person paying close attention to one student: moving at their pace, noticing what they missed, asking the next question at the right moment. But the current system is built around a compromise with one teacher managing thirty students.

Flint exists to take that compromise off the table. Personalized learning, at the scale of a whole school â every student working with something closer to a tutor, and every teacher able to see what's actually happening across their class instead of guessing.

Go look at the product before you read any further: app.flintk12.com

The Role

Students want something that stays with them, going at their pace and helps them get unstuck without just handing over the answer. Teachers want that happening inside a class they still control, and they'd like their evenings back. Admins want proof that the platform they rolled out is leading to teacher productivity and student progress.

Your job is to dive deep into this design problem, holding three sets of needs within one product. Weâll trust you to ship designs that are the best possible solution to our users most urgent pain points. tl;dr you'll get to own how Flint works and how it feels.

How We Work

• We move fast, and closely. You'll work with a small, senior team: one Product Lead, a Chief of Staff (Product), a CTO, and five engineers. We also have a running joke that we canât keep up with our #product_updates channel because of how much we ship.

• Fast and good aren't in tension here. In our experience the fastest route to something good is getting a rough version in front of a real teacher early, which tends to be quicker than getting it right in private. Decisions with the highest impact have often happened within days, not month long sprints.

• Weâre always learning. Call it on-brand or a bit on the nose, but learning from each other, our customers, the market have been key to our growth. We even have channels dedicated to sharing our workflow mistakes and wins. Education is also still being actively shaped as a field, and staying tuned to what users and the industry are telling us matters more than assuming we already know.

• Users drive our decisions. Our team isn't exclusively made up of former teachers, and that's deliberate. We'd rather build from real user feedback and a range of perspectives than from any one person's classroom experience. Our close connection with teachers, students, and admins helps us quickly understand what's working and what isn't.

• We design with AI, not around it. Lo-fi concepts out of Claude, prototypes we can put in front of a teacher the same week, PRDs drafted from screenshots and voice notes: these are just a few ways weâve used AI to support our work, and it's a real part of why our loop is as short as it is.

What You'll Do

• Dig deep, validate, and design. Validate the user goals, map key journeys, and land on the actual jobs to be done. People will hand you solutions along the way: the useful move is usually to find the need underneath before taking the solution at face value.

• Explore broadly, then narrow. Iteration is key. For a complex UI, we'd expect five or six real concepts on the table before committing to one, whether it sketches, wireframes, AI-generated lo-fi, competitor and industry researchâ¦whatever gets you there fastest. Then you cut it down with your own judgment, a review with someone on the team, and wherever we can manage it, real users.

• Design zero to one, and one to a hundred. Some of this is a genuinely new problem where you shape the whole thing from scratch. Some of it is taking something we shipped early and making it scalable, coherent, and delightful in the way the first version never had time to be.

• Communicate your judgment effectively. You can clearly explain the context, intent, designs, and the reasoning behind your work to the rest of the team.

• Set the design bar. Our design system and design philosophy are still taking form. You'll decide what becomes a pattern, what stays a one-off, and where the whole thing goes from here.

• Stay through QA and impact. You'll have a say in what gets QA'd and in what metrics tell us whether the thing actually worked. Shipping isn't the end of your involvement.

• Impact hundreds of thousands of learners. How a generation learns to think alongside AI is being decided right now, in the products that get built this year. Very few designers get to work on something this consequential this early.

What We're Looking For

• You've designed and shipped real software. We care far more about one thing you made and can talk us through than about ten polished case-study slides.

• You can run the whole arc, from understanding the problem through concepts, hi-fi, and a spec engineering can build from. Not every step has to be your strongest.

• You're comfortable with being scrappy and being iterative. You'd rather put a rough thing in front of a real teacher than a perfect thing in front of your own team.

• You want to shape a category-defining product. You're excited by building something that hasn't existed before and genuinely changes how people learn â not iterating on the margins of something that already works.

• You're here to learn, not just to apply what you already know. That means sharpening your design skills and process on the job, and getting deep on the education industry itself, from US private Kâ12 to foreign education ministries and everything in between. You find that range interesting rather than intimidating.

• You care about education. You should like what you are building and who you are building for!

What We Offer

• Meaningful equity.

• Health and dental insurance.

• Personal device stipend.

How to Apply

Message Sun with your resume and portfolio, or apply here.
